sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Hall County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Two Gainesville offices split the work. Appraisal belongs to the Board of Assessors; the Tax Commissioner mails the statements and takes payment. Neither sets the rate. Mill levies are voted by the county commissioners, the school board and each city that taxes on its own.

Hall County covers 429 square miles, 393 of them land, in the upper Piedmont just below the Blue Ridge foothills. The whole county makes up the Gainesville metro area, Gainesville is the county seat, and the Chattahoochee River gathers strength here on its way to Lake Sidney Lanier. The county was created in 1818, and the incorporated places are Gainesville, Buford, Flowery Branch, Oakwood, Lula, Gillsville, Braselton and Clermont. Most of the county sits in the Hall County School District, while parcels inside the city limits of Buford and Gainesville fall under those cities' own school systems, which changes the millage that applies.

Schools vary by address. High schools in the county include East Hall, North Hall, West Hall, Chestatee, Cherokee Bluff, Flowery Branch and Johnson with Gainesville High on the city side. Brenau University, Lanier Technical College and a University of North Georgia campus are all in Gainesville, and the Crescent train stops at the Amtrak station on Industrial Boulevard.

  • Assessment questions: Board of Assessors, 2875 Browns Bridge Road, Gainesville, 770.531.6720 for real property.
  • Billing and payment questions: Tax Commissioner, 770.531.6950 option 3, open Monday through Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • City bills: owners inside Gainesville, Flowery Branch, Buford, Braselton or Oakwood receive a second statement from that city.

sections.h2: When are Hall County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Sixty days after mailing is the rule in Hall. A normal season means a September 15 mailing and a November 15 deadline. The 2026 statements went out October 15, a month late because the state approval of the digest came late, so the deadline became December 15, 2026.

The county explains that the 60 day gap stays fixed even when the mailing slips, so a later bill gives you a later deadline. Interest starts building monthly once the deadline passes. Because the mailing date drives the deadline, plan around the date on your own statement.

Paying early is easy. The online portal at HallCountyTax.org shows payment status for every parcel and keeps records and receipts for the past ten years. Hall County lists E-Check as the cheapest route, at a flat $1.50. Expect 2.49% on a credit card and 1.50% on a debit card. You can also mail the pay slip to P.O. Box 1579, Gainesville, GA 30503, use the 24 hour drop box under the breezeway at the Government Center on Browns Bridge Road, or pay by phone with a card.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Hall County assessment?
sections.html:
Forty-five days from the date on the assessment notice is the limit. Hall takes appeals three ways: online in qPublic, by post to P.O. Box 2895, Gainesville, GA 30503, or at the counter at 2875 Browns Bridge Road.

If you do nothing in that window, the value goes to the Tax Commissioner for billing. The notices are mailed to every owner each year, and the 2026 digital copies were posted on qPublic.

Appealing never freezes the bill. Hall County sends an Under Appeal statement for the 2026 cycle, and the amount due by December 15, 2026 is the lower result of 85% of the 2026 value or 100% of the 2025 value. Any unpaid portion still accrues monthly interest from that date. Georgia's Department of Revenue notes that a refund after a final appeal decision is processed automatically, and that other refund claims for erroneous or illegal taxes must start within three years of payment.

sections.h2: What exemptions and filing deadlines apply in Hall County?
sections.html:
Filing season runs January 1 through April 1. Homestead applications, real property returns and personal property returns all use that window, and Hall County lets you do most of it online through qPublic.

  • Homestead exemptions, including the senior exemptions, the Total School Tax Exemption and the 100% Disabled Veteran exemption, are filed under the Real Property tab in qPublic.
  • Boats, personal watercraft, aircraft, business personal property and manufacturer personal property returns go under the Personal Property tab. Returns filed after April 1 carry a 10% late filing penalty.
  • Conservation Use covenants are the exception: they are taken in person at the Government Center, where an appointment is advised.

The state revenue department's Hall County fact sheet treats a missed homestead filing as a waiver. You may apply any time once the house is your primary residence, with April 1 as the cutoff for the first year of relief. Call 770.531.6720 about real property or 770.531.6749 about personal property.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when a Hall County house sells?
sections.html:
Hall County holds the January 1 owner of record answerable for that year's tax, even when the house changes hands in spring or summer. Who actually writes the check is a closing-table question, and the closing attorney handles it.

Hall County adds a step that sellers should not skip. If you sold real property during 2026, send the sales documents to the Tax Commissioner within 90 days of the due date, which works out to March 15, 2027. When the documents clearly shift liability to the new owner, the seller is no longer billed. Papers that arrive after March 15, 2027 cannot be considered. Boats, planes and business fixtures work the same way: whoever owned them in January stays on the hook after a sale.

Homeowners with an escrow account should know the county passes tax data to the mortgage servicer, yet the owner still answers for payment. Before listing, ask the Tax Commissioner what your parcel owes and hand that number to the closing attorney.

sections.h2: What do Hall County's numbers say about the housing market?
sections.html:
Of the four counties in this set, Hall is the priciest. Federal survey results for 2020 to 2024 give a typical owned home value of $350,400, household income of $80,901 and monthly rent of $1,341.

Growth since the April 2020 count comes to 11.7%. Owners with a mortgage typically spend $1,742 a month on housing, while owners with none spend $550. Hall County's 2025 permit count of 1,996 is far above the 24 recorded in Hancock County and 159 in Haralson County, a sign of where new construction is landing in this part of Georgia.

faqs.q: When do 2026 Hall County property taxes have to be paid?
faqs.a: The 2026 bills are due December 15, 2026. They were mailed October 15, and Hall County keeps the due date at 60 days after mailing. In a typical year the statements go out September 15 and fall due November 15.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to dispute a Hall County valuation?
faqs.a: The cutoff is 45 days after the date on the notice. Later, the value moves on to billing. Use qPublic, the P.O. Box 2895 mailing address, or the counter on Browns Bridge Road.

faqs.q: Can I pay Hall County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. HallCountyTax.org accepts E-Check for a flat $1.50, PayPal, and cards at 2.49% for credit and 1.50% for debit. You can also mail a check, use the Government Center drop box, or call 770.531.6950 to pay by card with an agent.

faqs.q: Who is billed for 2026 if my Hall County house sells?
faqs.a: The January 1, 2026 owner of record owes that year's tax, and the closing documents decide who actually pays. To move billing to the buyer, send the sales documents to the Tax Commissioner by March 15, 2027.

faqs.q: Do Hall County cities send their own tax bills?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners inside Gainesville, Flowery Branch, Buford, Braselton or Oakwood get a separate city statement in addition to the county bill. The county bill covers county and school levies only.
